assessment: The incumbent performs relatively well when assignments remain unchanged: median handling is seven minutes, versus 17 overall. Transition-linked selection or reconciliation errors are plausible because all eight affected exports involved assignment changes or renames, but causation is unproven. Execution takes only 40–75 seconds; replacement delays therefore do not establish slow generation. The concrete isolation limit is D1-O4: zero observed cross-center rows excludes the recently split-course center and cannot establish safety for that transition.

openings.claim: Resolving requested-week course membership through current assignments or mutable names may explain transition-linked omissions. Stable course identity with explicitly defined week membership is a candidate correction.
openings.delta: Move the investigation from rerunning exports to identifying which selection rule changes the intended course set.
openings.prediction: Holding attendance and the coordinator-confirmed intended set fixed, assignment changes or renames alter current output membership; a week-aware identity rule removes that difference. Absence of this effect weakens the hypothesis.
openings.probe: In private staging with fabricated participants, compare unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures against explicit expected sets. Include a second center and inspect every exported row for authorized-center membership. Preserve the documented CSV schema and verify concurrent attendance entry. Time-box diagnosis and any candidate implementation within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Historical membership may be unavailable; reconstruction feasibility must be established before selecting this correction.
Split-course membership needs an explicit expected result rather than inferred name matching.

openings.claim: Does excess coordinator handling arise primarily from course-set reconciliation, spreadsheet import, or repeated replacement requests?
openings.delta: Distinguish active handling from elapsed replacement delay before choosing a workflow change.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, observed checking and correction consume most excess active time. If import dominates, those steps remain costly even with a confirmed-correct course set; replacement waiting alone does not explain active handling.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators’ two short sessions with fabricated CSVs in authorized workspaces. Counterbalance confirmed-correct and transition-affected files; timestamp checking, correction, downloading, importing and requests separately, recording waiting separately. Compare intended sets with each coordinator’s actual schedule source.
assumptions: These sessions diagnose mechanisms; the next 40 exports must separately establish the stated success measures.
